skill.name: combat-ui-pattern-a
skill.description: Implement a split-panel combat interface for SHINOBI WAY with React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS. The skill covers layout structure, character panels, action docks, phase headers, VS dividers, styling tokens, and animation guidance.
skill.summary: Build a split-panel React combat UI with reusable game interface components.
skill.author: CesarAugustusGroB

content.value_statement: Combat screens are hard to split into clear player, enemy, and action zones. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a reusable React implementation guide.
actual_capabilities: Defines the Pattern A split-panel hierarchy for CombatLayout, PhaseHeader, ConfrontationZone, CharacterPanel, VSDivider, and ActionDock.
Maps existing Combat.tsx, PlayerHUD.tsx, and SkillCard.tsx sections to new reusable combat components.
Provides TypeScript prop interface references for player, enemy, skill, turn phase, and combat state data.
Specifies Tailwind CSS layout, color, spacing, card, button, resource bar, and responsive breakpoint tokens.
Describes animation hooks, keyframes, timing, screen shake, floating text, and reduced-motion support.
limitations: It is tailored to the SHINOBI WAY game structure and may need adaptation for other projects.
It provides implementation guidance, not a complete tested package.
It assumes React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS are already available.
It does not validate game balance, asset quality, or runtime performance.

use_cases.title: Refactor a Combat Screen
use_cases.description: Turn a crowded vertical combat scene into a split player-versus-enemy layout with reusable React components.

use_cases.title: Standardize Game UI Components
use_cases.description: Create shared panels, action cards, headers, and dividers that follow one combat interface pattern.

use_cases.title: Prototype Tactical Battle Flow
use_cases.description: Generate a clear combat layout that separates phase status, character state, and available actions.

prompt_templates.title: Create the Layout Shell
prompt_templates.prompt: Use combat-ui-pattern-a to build only the CombatLayout shell. Include responsive rows, imports, and props that match the existing project.

prompt_templates.title: Add the Phase Header
prompt_templates.prompt: Use combat-ui-pattern-a to implement PhaseHeader. Show turn number, current phase, side action count, and approach modifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Character Panels
prompt_templates.prompt: Use combat-ui-pattern-a to extract CharacterPanel from the existing player and enemy UI. Preserve health, chakra, buffs, identity, and alignment.

prompt_templates.title: Complete the Combat Interface
prompt_templates.prompt: Use combat-ui-pattern-a to migrate Combat.tsx to Pattern A. Implement layout, panels, action dock, VS divider, animations, and reduced-motion support.

output_examples.input: Build the Pattern A layout foundation for the combat scene.
output_examples.output: A generated CombatLayout plan with three regions, responsive mobile behavior, and clear mount points for header, confrontation zone, and action dock.

output_examples.input: Create reusable character panels for player and enemy data.
output_examples.output: A component design that supports mirrored alignment, identity display, resource bars, status effects, sprite presentation, and floating text anchors.

output_examples.input: Polish combat feedback and action controls.
output_examples.output: A UI implementation outline for quick actions, main actions, VS effects, screen shake, floating combat text, and reduced-motion alternatives.

best_practices: Start with CombatLayout before extracting smaller components.
Keep props aligned with the existing game state types.
Test responsive behavior and reduced-motion support during migration.
anti_patterns: Do not rewrite game logic while refactoring the combat interface.
Do not hardcode player or enemy values inside reusable components.
Do not remove the old combat layout before the new one is validated.

faq.question: What does this skill build?
faq.answer: It guides creation of a split-panel React combat UI for SHINOBI WAY.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it assume?
faq.answer: It assumes React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS are used in the target project.

faq.question: Can it generate all components at once?
faq.answer: Yes, but the workflow recommends starting with the layout shell and then extracting components.

faq.question: Does it include animation guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers keyframes, screen shake, floating text, timing, hooks, and reduced-motion handling.

faq.question: Is it limited to SHINOBI WAY?
faq.answer: The references are SHINOBI WAY specific, but the pattern can be adapted to other combat games.

faq.question: Does it include security-sensitive behavior?
faq.answer: No evidence of network access, secret handling, destructive commands, or prompt injection was found.
